subject.title: Feature: inbound 'reply in thread' / 'rit' user directive

question: Should OpenClaw make suffixes like `reply in thread` or `rit` a built-in cross-channel reply override, and what trigger vocabulary plus `replyToMode` override semantics are acceptable by default?
rationale: This is new product behavior rather than a broken current contract; the default vocabulary can silently alter delivery, and the optional config path would add public configuration surface.

options.title: Approve a narrow core directive
options.body: Adopt a small explicit suffix contract, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and require implementation to strip all model-facing and command-facing inbound body fields with threaded-channel coverage.

options.title: Keep it prompt or plugin owned
options.body: Leave natural-language phrasing to agent prompts or a plugin/API seam and keep core limited to explicit reply tags plus configured reply modes.

options.title: Require explicit config first
options.body: Allow the feature only behind a documented config key with schema, docs, and tests, accepting the extra configuration surface intentionally.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core directive
recommendation.body: Adopt a small explicit suffix contract, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and require implementation to strip all model-facing and command-facing inbound body fields with threaded-channel coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current signal on the shared inbound/reply-threading files and the product boundary is cross-channel core behavior.
